summary: PostgreSQL streaming replication is operational. node1 is the writable primary; node2 and node3 are read-only hot standbys. Replication uses the persistent WireGuard dbnet0 network (10.77.0.0/24), while PostgreSQL is unavailable on the management subnet.
actions_performed: Installed PostgreSQL 13 and WireGuard on all three nodes.
Created an encrypted full-mesh database network with node-generated keys.
Bound PostgreSQL only to loopback and each node's dbnet0 address.
Configured certificate-authenticated TLS streaming with dedicated physical slots.
Enabled PostgreSQL and dbnet0 services at boot.
Verified committed data on both standbys and confirmed standby writes are rejected.

evidence.requirement: node1 is the writable primary with two active streaming standbys
evidence.summary: node1 accepted a committed INSERT, reports recovery=false, and has TLS streaming connections from node2 and node3 with active physical slots and zero-byte replay lag.

evidence.requirement: Committed changes replicate to both standbys
evidence.summary: The identical committed row, including ID and timestamp, was observed on both recovery nodes.

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 are read-only standbys
evidence.summary: Both nodes report recovery=true and transaction_read_only=on, reject INSERT operations, and stream from node1 through their distinct slots.

evidence.requirement: Replication uses a dedicated database network
evidence.summary: dbnet0 is active at 10.77.0.1, 10.77.0.2, and 10.77.0.3 with fresh WireGuard handshakes, explicit overlay routes, and full peer reachability.

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL traffic remains off the management network
evidence.summary: Port 5432 is bound only to loopback/dbnet0 and allowed only in the database firewall zone. Live replication connections use 10.77.0.x; every management-address probe received no response while dbnet0 endpoints accepted connections.
PostgreSQL and dbnet0 are active and enabled on all nodes, with zero PostgreSQL configuration or HBA parsing errors.
